title: Generic smooth curve and etale boundary preparation over an excellent base
statement: Let $f:C\to B$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] dominant morphism of integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring] Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] schemes, whose generic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $Z\subset C$ be a proper closed subset [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There are integral excellent Noetherian schemes $C_0,B_0$, alterations $a:C_0\to C$ and $b:B_0\to B$, and a proper dominant morphism $f_0:C_0\to B_0$ with $f\circ a=b\circ f_0$ such that the generic fibre of $f_0$ is a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] geometrically integral curve [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and the reduced inverse image $Z_0=(a^{-1}Z)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is nowhere dense in $C_0$ with finite etale generic fibre [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] over $\kappa(B_0)$ [def-sc-generic-point]. An alteration means a proper surjective morphism finite over a dense open of its integral target.

source.place: Theorem 2.4 proof, §§2.7–2.10, especially Lemma 2.8 and normalization/spreading reductions, pp. 603–605. The preparation is over an arbitrary excellent Noetherian base; no projectivity or separatedness of the original base is used. Local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online.
